title: 第三章 市井百态录第四章 采花大盗
content_zh:
何成局把《阴阳缠绵诀》塞回灶台砖缝的时候，天边已经泛了鱼肚白。
他一夜没睡，眼睛布满了血丝，但精神却出奇地亢奋。那种感觉就像是一个饿了很久的人忽然闻到了肉香——还没吃到嘴里，但光是那股味道就足够让人打起精神来了。
他照常起床烧水煮粥，照常给姑娘们盛饭端茶，照常扫院子劈柴挑水。一切都跟往常一模一样，没有一个人发现他有任何不对劲。
这就是何成局的本事——六年跑堂练出来的。脸上笑嘻嘻，心里什么样，你永远看不出来。
辰时刚过，余三娘把他叫到了二楼账房。
龚文正趴在桌上算账，算盘珠子拨得噼里啪啦响。余三娘坐在窗边喝茶，手腕上那对翡翠镯子在晨光里绿得扎眼。
“成局，”余三娘放下茶杯，“今天你去一趟佛山。”
何成局愣了一下：“佛山？”
“钟铁山昨晚上落了一包银子在房里，足足五十两。”余三娘说这话的时候脸上没什么表情，但何成局注意到她的手指在茶杯沿上轻轻敲了两下——这是她心情不错时的小动作，“人家是佛山冶铁的大户，咱们不能贪这个便宜。你跑一趟，把银子给人送回去。”
何成局心里算了一下——从广州城到佛山镇，走官道大概四十里路，快走的话半天能到。来回就是八十里，加上在佛山找人交货的时间，得一整天。
“三娘，我一个人去？”
“怎么，怕被人劫了？”余三娘似笑非笑地看着他。
何成局挠了挠头，嘿嘿一笑：“我一条贱命不值钱，但五十两银子要是丢了，把我卖了都赔不起。”
“银子用布包好，揣在怀里，别露富。”余三娘站起身来，从柜子里取出一包用蓝布裹得严严实实的银锭，放在桌上，“早去早回，天黑之前必须回来。”
“是。”
何成局接过银包，掂了掂分量。五十两银子，沉甸甸的，压在手心里又凉又硬。他在春香楼干六年，攒下的全部家当也就三两多碎银。这一包够他不吃不喝攒上十几年。
他把银包塞进怀里，又摸了摸怀里的那本《阴阳缠绵诀》——他今天特意带在身上，怕放在厨房不安全。
一本书，一包银子，两样东西贴着他的胸口，一个轻如鸿毛，一个重如泰山。
何成局出了柳花巷，沿着大南门街往西走。官道在城西，穿过西门再走三十里就是佛山镇。
大清早的街道上人不算多，但该有的都有了——卖豆浆的小贩挑着担子沿街叫卖，几个半大孩子在巷口踢毽子，路边茶馆里三三两两的老人在喝茶下棋。

何成局走得不快不慢，步子轻快，心情也不坏。去佛山虽然累，但总比在春香楼里忙前忙后强，至少能看看外头的风景。
西门外的官道两边是一望无际的稻田。四月的稻子刚抽穗，绿油油的，风一吹就荡起一层层的波浪。何成局深吸了一口气，空气里有泥土和青草的味道，比柳花巷里的脂粉味和酒味好闻多了。
他走了大概十里路，官道上来往的人渐渐多了起来。有挑着担子进城卖菜的老农，有骑着高头大马匆匆赶路的驿卒，有赶着牛车运货的商贩，还有几个背着包袱、步履匆匆的旅人。
然后他看见了一个熟人。
也不能算熟人，但至少是张熟脸——城南那个叫黄彪的恶霸。
黄彪带着四个地痞正在官道上拦路。
他们的“拦路”倒也不是那种明目张胆的抢劫，而是更下作的招数——在官道拐弯处放了几块大石头，把路堵了一半。然后黄彪坐在路边的大石头上，嘴里叼着一根狗尾巴草，笑眯眯地看着被堵住的行人。想过去就得绕开石头，但旁边是稻田的泥水沟，过不去，只能搬石头。而搬石头的话……
“一块石头五十文。”黄彪伸出五根手指，冲着一个赶牛车的老农晃了晃。
老农都快哭了：“大爷，我这一车菜都卖不了五十文啊！”
“那就留两棵白菜抵账。”黄彪很好说话的样子。
何成局远远看见这一幕，脚下一顿，下意识地就想绕路。但他左右看了看，官道两边都是稻田，绕不过去，除非踩进泥水里趟过去。
他皱了皱眉，硬着头皮继续往前走。
黄彪是老熟人了。这家伙是城南的地头蛇，炼体境一层的武者，手下聚了二十多个地痞，专干收保护费和拦路讹诈的勾当。他偶尔也会光顾春香楼——虽然余三娘很不待见他，但做生意嘛，只要给银子，什么人都得招待。
何成局在春香楼给黄彪端过好几次茶，算是有几分薄面。但这点薄面值不值五十文，他不敢保证。
“哟，这不是春香楼的小二哥吗？”
果然，黄彪一眼就认出了他。
何成局脸上立刻堆起笑容，快走几步迎上去，弯腰作了个揖：“黄爷早，您今儿个怎么在这儿呢？”
黄彪把嘴里的狗尾巴草换了个方向，上下打量了何成局一眼：“你小子不在春香楼端盘子，跑佛山去干嘛？”
“给三娘跑腿，送点东西。”何成局说这话的时候下意识地按了按胸口，确保银包没露出来。
这个动作没有逃过黄彪的眼睛。
content_en:
When He Chengju stuffed "Yin Yang Ling Jue" back into the cracks of the stove bricks, the sky was already turning white.
He hadn't slept all night, his eyes were bloodshot, but his energy was surprisingly high. It feels like a person who has been hungry for a long time and suddenly smells the aroma of meat - it hasn't been eaten yet, but the smell alone is enough to cheer people up.
He got up as usual to boil water and cook porridge, served rice and tea to the girls as usual, swept the yard, chopped firewood and carried water as usual. Everything was exactly as usual, no one noticed anything wrong with him.
This is He Chengju's ability - developed from six years of training as a waiter. You can never tell what’s going on in your heart despite the smile on your face.
Just after Chen hour, Yu Sanniang called him to the accounting room on the second floor.
Gong Wen was lying on the table calculating accounts, and the beads on the abacus were crackling. Yu Sanniang was sitting by the window drinking tea. The pair of jade bracelets on her wrists were dazzlingly green in the morning light.
"Sure," Yu Sanniang put down her tea cup, "Today you go to Foshan."
He Chengju was stunned for a moment: "Foshan?"
"Zhong Tieshan left a bag of silver in the room last night, a total of fifty taels." There was no expression on Yu Sanniang's face when she said this, but He Chengju noticed that her fingers tapped the rim of the teacup twice - this was a small gesture she did when she was in a good mood. "They are a big iron smelting company in Foshan, and we can't take advantage of this. You go over and send the silver back."
He Chengju made a mental calculation - from Guangzhou City to Foshan Town, it takes about forty miles via the official road. If you walk quickly, you can get there in half a day. The round trip is eighty miles, plus the time it takes to find someone to deliver the goods in Foshan, it takes a whole day.
"Sanniang, should I go alone?"
"What, are you afraid of being robbed?" Yu Sanniang looked at him with a half-smile.
He Chengju scratched his head and chuckled: "My life is worthless, but if I lose fifty taels of silver, I can't even afford to pay for it if I sell it."
"Wrap the silver in cloth and put it in your arms. Don't show your wealth." Yu Sanniang stood up, took out a package of silver ingots wrapped tightly in blue cloth from the cabinet, and placed it on the table. "Go early and come back early. You must be back before dark."
"Yes."
He Chengju took the wallet and weighed it. Fifty taels of silver, heavy, cold and hard in the palm of my hand. He worked in Chunxiang Tower for six years, and all he had saved was only three taels of silver. This bag is enough for him to save for more than ten years without eating or drinking.
He stuffed his wallet into his arms and touched the book "Yin Yang Ling Jue" - he brought it with him today because he was afraid it would be unsafe in the kitchen.
A book and a bag of silver were placed against his chest, one as light as a feather and the other as heavy as a mountain.
He Chengju left Liuhua Lane and walked west along Dananmen Street. The official road is in the west of the city. After passing through the west gate and walking thirty miles further, you will reach Foshan Town.
There weren't many people on the street in the early morning, but there were everything there was to see - vendors selling soy milk carried burdens along the street, a few half-year-old children were playing shuttlecock at the alley, and old people in twos and threes were drinking tea and playing chess in roadside teahouses.
He Chengju walked neither fast nor slowly, with brisk steps and in a good mood. Although going to Foshan is tiring, it is better than rushing around in Chunxiang Tower. At least you can see the scenery outside.
On both sides of the official road outside the west gate are endless rice fields. The rice in April has just eared and is green, with layers of waves swaying when the wind blows. He Chengju took a deep breath. The air smelled of earth and grass, much better than the smell of powder and wine in Liuhua Lane.
He walked about ten miles, and gradually more and more people came and went on the official road. There are old farmers carrying burdens into the city to sell vegetables, postmen riding tall horses in a hurry, vendors driving oxcarts to transport goods, and a few travelers carrying baggage in a hurry.
Then he saw an acquaintance.
He couldn't be considered an acquaintance, but at least he had a familiar face - the bully named Huang Biao from the south of the city.
Huang Biao and four gangsters were blocking the road on the official road.
Their "blocking"It's not that kind of blatant robbery, but a more despicable trick - placing a few big rocks at the corner of the official road, blocking the road halfway. Then Huang Biao sat on the big stone on the side of the road, holding a piece of dogtail grass in his mouth, and looked at the blocked pedestrians with a smile. If he wanted to get past, he had to go around the stone, but there was a muddy ditch in the rice field next to it. If he couldn't get through, he could only move the stone. And if he moved the stone...
"One stone costs fifty cents. "Huang Biao stretched out five fingers and shook them at an old farmer driving a bullock cart.
The old farmer was about to cry: "Uncle, I can't even sell this cart of vegetables for fifty cents!" "
"Then leave two cabbages to offset the debt. "Huang Biao is very talkative.
When He Chengju saw this scene from a distance, he stopped and subconsciously wanted to take a detour. But he looked around and saw that there were rice fields on both sides of the official road. He couldn't get around it unless he stepped into the muddy water and waded through.
He frowned and continued to move forward.
Huang Biao is an old acquaintance. This guy is a local gangster in the south of the city, a warrior at the first level of the Body Refining Realm. He has more than twenty gangsters under him, specializing in collecting protection fees and blocking roads for blackmail. He would occasionally visit Chunxiang Tower - although Yu Sanniang didn't like to see him, but in business, as long as you give money, you have to entertain everyone.
He Chengju served Huang Biao several teas at Chunxiang Tower, which was considered a bit thin. But he couldn't guarantee whether this thin face value was worth fifty cents.
"Hey, isn't this the second brother from Chunxiang Tower? "
Sure enough, Huang Biao recognized him at a glance.
He Chengju immediately put a smile on his face, walked a few steps to meet him, bent down and bowed: "Good morning, Mr. Huang, why are you here today? "
Huang Biao changed the direction of the dog's tail grass in his mouth and looked He Chengju up and down: "Why are you going to Foshan if you don't serve the dishes at Chunxiang Tower? "
“Run errands for Sanniang and give me something. "When He Chengju said this, he subconsciously pressed his chest to ensure that the wallet was not exposed.
This action did not escape Huang Biao's eyes.
